mainTopic: רבי יהודה on נדר vs. נדבה, whether a נזיר is a sinner, and the substitute words for vows
overview: The amud opens by showing that our משנה, which praises a נדבה (freewill offering) but not a נדר (vow), can follow רבי יהודה. The גמרא reads his ברייתא as praising נודב, not נודר. It explains that a נדבה carries no risk of a stumbling block, because רבי יהודה lets a person consecrate his animal in the עזרה and offer it at once. For volunteering נזירות, רבי יהודה cites the early חסידים, who became נזירים so they could bring a קרבן חטאת. רבי שמעון disagrees and says they avoided נזירות because a נזיר is called a sinner. אביי then groups שמעון הצדיק, רבי שמעון and רבי אלעזר הקפר as all holding that a נזיר is a sinner. רבי אלעזר הקפר learns from this that anyone who fasts without need is called a sinner. A new משנה then lists substitute words (כינויין) for קרבן, חרם, נזירות and שבועה. רבי יוחנן says these are foreign words, while ריש לקיש says the חכמים invented them so that people would not come to say God's name in vain. A ברייתא of רבי שמעון begins, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Our משנה can follow רבי יהודה, who only praised freewill offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה could match רבי יהודה. He only praised a נדבה, never a נדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the משנה follows רבי יהודה. When רבי יהודה said it is good to vow and fulfill, he meant a freewill offering (נדבה). About a vow (נדר) he did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its earlier question about whose view the משנה follows. It says the משנה can match רבי יהודה if we limit what he praised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that רבי יהודה seemed to praise even vows, while the משנה says proper people avoid vows. The answer narrows his praise to נדבה only. So רבי יהודה and the משנה now agree: נדבה is good, נדר is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say; it introduces a way to fit a source to a certain opinion
A freewill offering: setting aside a specific animal ("this one is an offering")
A vow: taking on an obligation ("it is upon me to bring an offering")

steps.confusionAlert: Here נדר and נדבה are two different kinds of offering pledges. A נדר is a general obligation on the person. A נדבה is a specific animal set aside. Don't read them as the same thing.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Yehuda,
when Rabbi Yehuda spoke, it was about a freewill offering;
about a vow he did not say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question of whose view the משנה follows
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of an opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה praised vows too, so he cannot be the author of the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה only praised נדבה, which fits the משנה

steps.title: But the ברייתא says רבי יהודה praised one who vows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה praising a נודר, one who vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't the ברייתא teach in רבי יהודה's name: "Better than both this and that is one who vows and fulfills"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 1 by quoting רבי יהודה's actual words in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the word נודר, "vows." That seems to show רבי יהודה praised real vows, not only freewill offerings. If so, the limit from step 1 does not fit his words.

keyTerms.meaning: But doesn't it teach…? This opens a challenge from a source
One who vows and fulfills

phrases.english: But doesn't it teach: "Better than both this and that
phrases.notes: "This and that" means the two options in the ברייתא: not vowing, and vowing without fulfilling.

phrases.english: is one who vows and fulfills"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה only praised נדבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's wording "נודר" shows he praised vows

steps.title: Correct the wording: "one who volunteers and fulfills"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the word in the ברייתא from נודר to נודב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it this way: "one who volunteers (a freewill offering) and fulfills."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by fixing the wording of רבי יהודה's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two Hebrew words differ by just one letter: נודר (vows) and נודב (volunteers). By reading נודב, רבי יהודה's praise is only for נדבה. So the answer from step 1 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: One who volunteers a freewill offering

phrases.english: Teach: "one who volunteers and fulfills."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says נודר, meaning vows
steps.terutzMaskana: Read it as נודב, meaning freewill offerings

steps.title: Why should a freewill offering be better than a vow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the stumbling-block worry applies to a נדבה just as much as to a נדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about one who vows, that he should not, because perhaps he will come to a stumbling block with it? A freewill offering too: perhaps he will come to a stumbling block with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the difference between נדר and נדבה. It asks why the risk that rules out a vow does not also rule out a freewill offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vowing is discouraged because the person might fail to bring the offering in time, which is a תקלה (stumbling block). But a person who sets aside a specific animal could also delay or mishandle it. So why should רבי יהודה praise נדבה at all?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? A challenge to a distinction
A stumbling block; here, coming to sin with the offering
Perhaps; it raises a worry

phrases.english: What is different about one who vows, that he should not vow,
because perhaps he will come to a stumbling block with it?
phrases.notes: The worry is that he might put off bringing the offering and break the rule against delaying.

phrases.english: A freewill offering too,
perhaps he will come to a stumbling block with it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the logic behind the distinction set up in steps 1 and 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between נדר and נדבה in רבי יהודה's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same risk of a stumbling block exists in both cases

steps.title: רבי יהודה lets a person consecrate and offer his animal right away
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה follows his own view: a person can consecrate his lamb in the עזרה and offer it at once, so there is no risk.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה follows his own reasoning, for he said: A person brings his lamb to the Temple courtyard, consecrates it, leans on it, and slaughters it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to another ruling of רבי יהודה. It shows that a נדבה can be done with no delay at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a נדבה, the person can wait until he is already in the עזרה to make the animal holy. Then he does סמיכה and slaughters it right away, so there is no time for a stumbling block. A נדר is a general obligation that hangs on the person, so the risk of delay remains.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning that he holds elsewhere
The Temple courtyard
Leans his hands on the animal (סמיכה) before slaughter
Makes it holy as an offering

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, a נדבה is praiseworthy and a נדר is not. A נדבה can be consecrated and offered on the spot in the עזרה, so it carries no risk of a stumbling block. That is how the משנה can follow רבי יהודה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the משנה's praise of נדבה, but not נדר, fits with רבי יהודה's view.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning, for he said:
A person brings his lamb to the Temple courtyard,
consecrates it, leans on it, and slaughters it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to the author's own consistent view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נדבה carries the same risk of a stumbling block as a נדר
steps.terutzMaskana: A נדבה can be consecrated and offered immediately in the עזרה, so it has no risk

steps.title: The answer works for offerings, but what about volunteering נזירות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the answer for a נדבה of קרבנות, but asks how it can work for a נדבה of נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, that answer works for a voluntary gift of offerings. But what can you say about volunteering to become a נזיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 5. That answer works for animal offerings, but it does not seem to work for volunteering to be a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a קרבן, a person can consecrate his animal in the עזרה and offer it right away, so there is no time to stumble. נזירות is different: it lasts many days, and during that time he could break its rules. So the worry about a stumbling block comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: That works out fine (for this case)
A voluntary gift, something a person takes on freely
Being a נזיר: no wine, no haircut, no contact with the dead, for a set time

phrases.english: That works for a voluntary gift of offerings,
but for a voluntary gift of nazirite-hood, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח נְדָבָה דְקׇרְבָּנוֹת, נְדָבָה דִנְזִירוּת מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 5's answer for offerings but says it does not cover נזירות.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 5's claim that רבי יהודה sees no stumbling-block risk in a נדבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'offer it at once' answer only works when the obligation can be done right away. נזירות stretches over time, so the risk of breaking it remains.

steps.title: רבי יהודה praises volunteering נזירות: the early חסידים did it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה follows his own view: the early חסידים volunteered נזירות so that they would be obligated to bring a קרבן חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה follows his own view. A ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says the early pious people longed to bring a קרבן חטאת. But ה׳ never let them sin, so they had no reason to bring one. What did they do? They volunteered to become נזירים, so they would have to bring the נזיר's קרבן חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that רבי יהודה himself holds that volunteering נזירות is a good thing. It quotes a ברייתא about the early חסידים to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's view, the early חסידים chose to volunteer נזירות. So for him, a נדבה of נזירות is praiseworthy, just like a נדבה of קרבנות. That fits the claim that the משנה, which praises a נדבה, follows רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, his known view elsewhere
The early pious people of earlier generations
A stumbling block, here meaning even an accidental sin
A sin-offering

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that in רבי יהודה's view, נזירות is something pious people chose to take on, and not something to stay away from.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning.
As it was taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The early pious people
would long to bring a sin-offering.
Because the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not
bring a stumbling block through them,
phrases.notes: He means they never sinned, even by accident, so they never had a chance to bring a חטאת.

phrases.english: what would they do?
They would rise and volunteer nazirite-hood to God,
so that he would become obligated in a sin-offering to God.
phrases.notes: A נזיר brings a חטאת among his offerings, so becoming a נזיר gave them a way to bring one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by showing that רבי יהודה approves of volunteering נזירות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the תנא in question holds this view elsewhere (לטעמיה), using a ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נדבה of נזירות should be discouraged, because it lasts a long time and he might break it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה holds that the early חסידים volunteered נזירות, so for him it is a praiseworthy נדבה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the חסידים brought voluntary offerings but avoided נזירות
steps.stepSummary: In the same ברייתא, רבי שמעון disagrees. The חסידים volunteered עולה, שלמים and תודה, but not נזירות, so they would not be called sinners.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: they did not vow to be נזירים. Instead, anyone who wanted to bring an עולה volunteered and brought it. The same went for שלמים, and for a תודה with its four kinds of bread. But they did not volunteer נזירות, so they would not be called sinners, as the פסוק says about a נזיר: 'and he shall atone for him for having sinned regarding the soul.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי שמעון, who argues on רבי יהודה. He says the early חסידים stayed away from נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון agrees the חסידים gave voluntary offerings, but only regular ones like עולה, שלמים and תודה. He holds that a נזיר is called a sinner, because the תורה speaks of atonement for a נזיר 'for having sinned.' So becoming a נזיר was something they avoided.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt-offering, burned completely on the מזבח
A peace-offering, shared by the מזבח, the כהנים and the owner
A thanks-offering, brought with breads
Sinners

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not saying the חסידים avoided voluntary offerings. They gave plenty of them. They only avoided נזירות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
They did not vow nazirite-hood,
rather: one who wanted to bring a burnt-offering
would volunteer and bring it,
a peace-offering — he would volunteer and bring it,
a thanks-offering and its four kinds of bread
he would volunteer and bring it.
But they did not volunteer nazirite-hood,
so that they would not be called sinners.
As it says: "And he shall atone for him
for having sinned regarding the soul."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: לֹא נָדְרוּ בְּנָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא goes on to give רבי שמעון's opposing view to רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The early חסידים volunteered regular offerings but not נזירות, because a נזיר is called a sinner (במדבר 6:11).

steps.title: אביי: three תנאים agree that a נזיר is a sinner
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that שמעון הצדיק, רבי שמעון and רבי אלעזר הקפר all hold that a נזיר is a sinner. He points out that the sources for שמעון הצדיק and רבי שמעון were already quoted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: שמעון הצדיק, רבי שמעון and רבי אלעזר הקפר all hold the same view, that a נזיר is a sinner. For שמעון הצדיק and רבי שמעון, we already saw their sources.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי groups three תנאים who share one view: a נזיר counts as a sinner. He sets up the next step, where the גמרא will bring the source for רבי אלעזר הקפר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sources for שמעון הצדיק and רבי שמעון were already brought. רבי שמעון's is the ברייתא just quoted. Only רבי אלעזר הקפר's source is still missing, and that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: An early כהן גדול, whose view on a נזיר was quoted earlier
One shared view
That which we already said

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה praises volunteering נזירות. רבי שמעון avoids it because a נזיר is called a sinner. אביי lists three תנאים who hold that a נזיר is a sinner.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Shimon HaTzaddik and Rabbi Shimon
and Rabbi Elazar HaKappar
all hold one view,
that a nazirite is a sinner:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁמְעוֹן הַצַּדִּיק וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הָא דַּאֲמַרַן.
phrases.english: Shimon HaTzaddik and Rabbi Shimon, that is what we already said.
phrases.notes: שמעון הצדיק's view came earlier in the גמרא, and רבי שמעון's is the ברייתא we just learned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: שִׁמְעוֹן הַצַּדִּיק וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר כּוּלָּן שִׁיטָה אַחַת הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי שמעון's view in step 8 and groups him with other תנאים who hold the same view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמעון הצדיק, רבי שמעון and רבי אלעזר הקפר all hold that a נזיר is a sinner. The first two sources were already quoted, and the third is still to come.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר הקפר's source: the נזיר sinned by holding back from wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows רבי אלעזר הקפר holds a נזיר is a sinner. The פסוק says the כהן atones for the נזיר's sin 'against the soul', which means he made himself suffer by giving up wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר הקפר also holds this. A ברייתא teaches that he said: the פסוק says, 'And he shall atone for him, for that he sinned against the soul.' Which soul did he sin against? He sinned by making himself suffer when he held back from wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the third source for אביי's statement. This is the ברייתא of רבי אלעזר הקפר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the sources for שמעון הצדיק and רבי שמעון were already quoted. Now he supplies the missing source for רבי אלעזר הקפר. The phrase 'sinned against the soul' is puzzling, since the נזיר hurt no one, so רבי אלעזר הקפר explains that the 'soul' is the נזיר's own self, which he denied wine.

keyTerms.meaning: A title of honor for a distinguished scholar
'And he shall atone for him' (the כהן atoning for the נזיר)
Sinned against the soul
Made himself suffer

steps.whyThisMatters: This completes אביי's list of three תנאים who see נזירות as a kind of sin.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar HaKappar the Distinguished
as it is taught in a ברייתא
Rabbi Elazar HaKappar the Distinguished says
"And he shall atone for him
for that he sinned against the soul"
Against which soul did this one sin?
Rather, he sinned by making himself suffer when he held back from wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the third name in אביי's list.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that רבי אלעזר הקפר holds a נזיר is a sinner
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא reading of 'חטא על הנפש' (במדבר 6:11)

steps.title: A קל וחומר: whoever fasts without need is called a sinner
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר הקפר continues. If a person who only gives up wine is called a sinner, then someone who gives up everything is even more so a sinner. So anyone who fasts is called a sinner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this a קל וחומר? This נזיר made himself suffer only by holding back from wine, and he is called a sinner. Someone who makes himself suffer by holding back from everything is all the more so a sinner. From here we learn that anyone who sits in a fast is called a sinner.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר הקפר takes his reading of the פסוק one step further. He uses a קל וחומר to teach a rule about fasting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The small case is the נזיר, who gives up only wine. The big case is the person who fasts, who gives up all food and drink. If the small case already counts as a sin, the big case surely does.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
All the more so
One who sits in a fast
A sinner

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean every fast is forbidden. The point is that taking on suffering for no reason has a downside.

phrases.english: And are these matters not a קל וחומר?
Just as this one, who made himself suffer
only by holding back from wine, is called a sinner,
then one who makes himself suffer by holding back from everything
is all the more so a sinner.
From here we learn that anyone who sits in a fast
is called a sinner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the reading of the פסוק to a general rule about fasting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone who fasts without need is called a sinner, learned by קל וחומר from the נזיר.

steps.title: The פסוק is about a נזיר who became טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר הקפר. The פסוק about atoning for sin is written about a נזיר who became טמא, so maybe only that נזיר is called a sinner.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this פסוק is written about a נזיר who became טמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof from the פסוק. It points out that the פסוק is talking about a specific kind of נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק speaks only of a נזיר who became טמא, then his 'sin' may simply be becoming טמא during his נזירות. In that case there is no proof that an ordinary נזיר is a sinner.

keyTerms.meaning: A נזיר who became ritually impure
This פסוק

phrases.english: But this verse
is written about a נזיר who became טמא!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר הקפר's reading of 'חטא על הנפש'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק's context is a נזיר who became טמא, so the 'sin' may be the impurity, not the נזירות itself.

steps.title: The impure נזיר sinned a second time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the impure נזיר is called a sinner there because he repeated his sin. Becoming a נזיר was already a sin, and the impurity added to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says this about him because he sinned a second time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר הקפר. It explains why the word 'sin' shows up specifically in the case of the impure נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The impure נזיר has to restart his נזירות, so he goes back into the suffering of not drinking wine. That is why the תורה mentions sin in his case, but the basic sin is the נזירות itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Repeated a sin

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר הקפר, becoming a נזיר is itself counted as a sin. The impure נזיר is mentioned in the פסוק only because he sinned twice.

phrases.english: It is because he repeated his sin.
phrases.notes: The גמרא means that by becoming impure, he has to start his נזירות again, so he sins a second time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting why the פסוק mentions sin in this case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק calls only the impure נזיר a sinner, because he became impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: Every נזיר is a sinner. The impure נזיר is singled out because he repeated the sin.

steps.title: The משנה: substitute words for קרבן, חרם, נזירות and שבועה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists made-up or altered words that work like the real words of a vow. קונם, קונח and קונס stand for קרבן. חרק, חרך and חרף stand for חרם. נזיק, נזיח and פזיח stand for נזירות. שבותה, שקוקה and מוהי stand for שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'קונם', 'קונח' or 'קונס', these are substitute words for 'קרבן'. 'חרק', 'חרך' and 'חרף' are substitute words for 'חרם'. 'נזיק', 'נזיח' and 'פזיח' are substitute words for 'נזירות'. 'שבותה', 'שקוקה', or someone who vows with 'מוהי', these are substitute words for 'שבועה'.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists substitute words (כינויין) for four kinds of vows and teaches that each one works like the real word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה taught that substitute words work. Now it gives the actual list for each category. There are three substitutes for each of the first three categories, and for שבועה there are two words plus vowing with 'מוהי'.

keyTerms.meaning: Substitute words that stand in for the real term
A common substitute word for קרבן
Dedicating something to the בית המקדש or to כהנים
The state of being a נזיר
An oath
A word used as a substitute for שבועה

phrases.english: MISHNAH
One who says (to his fellow)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: "konam", "konach" or "konas"
these are substitute words for "korban" (offering).
"cherek", "cherech" or "cheref"
these are substitute words for "cherem" (dedication).
"nazik", "naziach" or "paziach"
these are substitute words for being a nazir.
"shevutah" or "shekukah",
or one who vows with "mohi"
these are substitute words for an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins and the topic shifts to substitute words for vows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These altered words work just like the real words קרבן, חרם, נזירות and שבועה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the substitute words come from foreign languages
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא records a dispute about כינויין. רבי יוחנן says they are real words from the languages of other nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated about substitute words: רבי יוחנן said that they are the language of the nations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with a dispute between אמוראים. This step brings the first side, רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that words like קונם are not invented. They are the actual words for קרבן and the rest in other languages, so a vow made with them is like a vow in a different language.

keyTerms.meaning: The language of other nations

phrases.english: GEMARA
It was stated about substitute words:
Rabbi Yochanan said:
They are the language of the nations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's explanation of the משנה's כינויין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כינויין are real words for vows taken from foreign languages.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the חכמים made up these words
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש disagrees. He says the חכמים invented these words so that people could vow with them, and he shows from a פסוק that 'בדא' means to make up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: it is a language that the חכמים made up for people to vow with. And so the פסוק says, 'In the month that he made up in his own heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second side of the dispute. ריש לקיש explains the כינויין differently and backs up the meaning of his word with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, these words have no meaning in any language. The חכמים created them as a way to vow, perhaps so people would not say the holy word itself. He quotes the פסוק about ירבעם to show that 'בדא' means inventing something from one's own mind.

keyTerms.meaning: Made up, invented
And so the פסוק says (brings support from a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute: רבי יוחנן says כינויין are foreign words, and ריש לקיש says the חכמים invented them for vowing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
It is a language that the Sages made up
for a person to vow with it.
And so the verse says:
"In the month that he made up in his own heart."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 12:33. It is about ירבעם, and it shows that the word בדא means to make something up.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: לָשׁוֹן שֶׁבָּדוּ לָהֶם חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כינויין are words the חכמים invented for making vows.

steps.title: Why did the חכמים invent substitute words?
steps.stepSummary: According to ריש לקיש, the חכמים made up כינויין. The גמרא asks what their reason was.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason the חכמים set up substitute words?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that follows from ריש לקיש's view in Step 16: if the חכמים invented these words, why did they bother?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's view needs no reason, because the words already exist in other languages. ריש לקיש says the חכמים created them on purpose, so there must be a purpose. The גמרא now looks for it.

keyTerms.meaning: the reason
they set up, established
substitute words used in place of the real vow words

phrases.english: And what is the reason
phrases.notes: This question follows ריש לקיש's view that the חכמים made these words up.

phrases.english: that the Rabbis established substitute words?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind ריש לקיש's claim in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the חכמים would invent substitute vow words.

steps.title: So that a person will not say the word קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The reason is so that a person will not say 'קרבן' itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that he will not say 'קרבן'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the substitute words exist so that a person will use them and avoid saying the actual word 'קרבן'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a substitute like קונם, a person can make his vow without saying the real word. The גמרא has not yet said what is wrong with saying 'קרבן'. That is the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: an offering; the main word used to make something forbidden by a vow

phrases.english: So that he should not say 'offering.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כינויין let a person avoid saying the actual word 'קרבן'.

steps.title: What is wrong with saying קרבן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: let him just say 'קרבן'. Why is that a problem?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him say 'קרבן'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. Saying 'קרבן' seems harmless, so why avoid it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 18 only moved the question back one step. Unless saying 'קרבן' causes some harm, there is still no reason to invent new words.

keyTerms.meaning: but let him say

phrases.english: But let him say 'offering'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the כינויין exist to avoid saying 'קרבן'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No harm in saying 'קרבן' has been shown, so avoiding it gives no real reason.

steps.title: He might say 'an offering to the Lord'
steps.stepSummary: The concern is that once he says 'קרבן', he may add 'to the Lord'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he will say 'an offering to the Lord'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: someone who uses the word קרבן might say the full phrase 'קרבן לה׳', the way the תורה says it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that God's name will come into the vow. Exactly why that is a problem is spelled out two steps later.

keyTerms.meaning: perhaps, maybe
an offering to the Lord (includes God's name)

phrases.english: Perhaps he will say 'an offering to the Lord.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19.
steps.terutzMaskana: Saying 'קרבן' could lead to adding God's name.

steps.title: What is wrong with saying קרבן לה׳?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes again: let him say 'קרבן לה׳'. That is how the פסוק says it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him say 'קרבן לה׳'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. Even saying 'קרבן לה׳' seems fine, so what is the danger?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'קרבן לה׳' is a proper, meaningful use of God's name. It is not wasteful, so the danger still has not been shown.

phrases.english: But let him say 'an offering to the Lord'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The concern that he will say 'קרבן לה׳'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying God's name together with an offering is a proper use, so no sin has been shown.

steps.title: He might say God's name and never finish
steps.stepSummary: The real danger: he might say 'לה׳' first, change his mind, never say 'קרבן', and so say God's name for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he will say 'to the Lord' and not say 'קרבן', and he will be saying the Name of Heaven for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer: a person might start with God's name, stop before saying 'קרבן', and end up saying שם שמים for nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain is now complete. כינויין prevent saying 'קרבן', which prevents adding 'לה׳', which prevents a half-finished vow where God's name is said for no purpose. Each step guards against the next danger.

keyTerms.meaning: brings out, says aloud
the Name of Heaven, God's name
for nothing, in vain

steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש, the חכמים invented כינויין as a fence, so that people would never come to say God's name in vain while making a vow.

phrases.english: Perhaps he will say 'to the Lord'
phrases.notes: He means he says God's name first, before the word 'offering'.

phrases.english: and not say 'offering,'
and he will be uttering the Name of Heaven in vain.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא אָמַר לַה׳ וְלָא אָמַר קׇרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21 and finishes the explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the final danger behind the chain
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying 'קרבן לה׳' is a proper use of God's name.
steps.terutzMaskana: The danger is saying 'לה׳' first and never finishing, which means saying God's name in vain.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains, according to ריש לקיש, why the חכמים created the משנה's substitute words at all: they are a protective stand-in for the real words.

steps.title: Support from a ברייתא of רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to quote a ברייתא from רבי שמעון that supports the idea of avoiding God's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון says:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is introducing a ברייתא from רבי שמעון, and the actual quote comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ותניא' shows that a supporting source is coming for the concern about saying God's name. The content of רבי שמעון's teaching comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: And it is taught: Rabbi Shimon says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a supporting source for the concern raised in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: The concern about saying God's name before finishing the vow.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון (continues on the next amud).
